OK, I'll give you the short answer. 3D printers are really good at making prototypes. But they lack a lot of qualities a super resilient Mars colony would need. For instance. 3D printed items have very low structural integrity compared to an injected molded part. You can't trust your life, let alone every life in the colony to a 3D printed part.

Then you need to source the materials. There is no oil on Mars, therefore, no plastic. And even if there were oil on Mars, there is no logistical infrastructure to get at the hypothetical oil and no logistical infrastrucure to transport the oil. and no refinery. and no factory to make filliments. And that's only for the plastic parts. You still don't have a way of sourcing silicon for the solar panel you are supposedly building, or a mine to source ore for metal, or a metal refinery. etc... etc... etc.

So, as long as you need to source ALL of your materials from Earth, you might as well just manufacture them on Earth. Because the real cost is going to be launch costs, which is usually determined by the weight of the material anyway. The weight of a solar panel is the same as the weight for the materials to make a solar panel. The launch cost is the same regardless of it being manufactured on Earth or just raw material, so just ship the pre-manufactured good.

Then add on to the problem the fact that 3D printing is extremely slow. So, to make any real progress, you'd have to launch thousands of 3D printers. And you might as well have just sent the things that need to be printed instead.

There might be a couple of 3D printers in the colony to make some things, maybe a part for a temporary fix if a knob breaks or something. But largely, everything will be imported pre-fabricated from Earth.
